title: Standard Form 1: Converting
summary: Why we use standard form, and converting large and small numbers both ways. The method: write the number as a smaller number times a power of ten, make the first number between 1 and 10, combine the tens; the place value grid then gives the quicker rule (down a place, power up 1). Numbers in parts sit inside each section. Printed Sheets 1 and 2 are placeholders. All questions are authored.

els.text: Why we use it, and converting
Write large and small numbers in standard form, and convert them back.

•  Say why standard form is used
•  Say whether a number is in standard form
•  Convert large and small numbers both ways

Short, and the size is easy to see.
2.  It is hard to miscount: no rows of zeros.
3.  The power shows the size at a glance.
Your calculator switches to it when the answer will not fit on the screen.

A number is in standard form when it is written as

$A \times 10^{n}$

where $1 \le A < 10$ and $n$ is an integer.

els.text:
•  Standard form is $A \times 10^{n}$ with $1 \le A < 10$ and $n$ an integer.
•  Write the number as $A$ times a 1 with zeros, then as a power of ten; or peel off one ten at a time.
•  Down one place, the power goes up by $1$. Up one place, the power goes down by $1$.
•  Small numbers: divide by tens, so the power is negative.
